Part 1

How do you read a cause & effect matrix?

Part 1 · the plan

Rows are causes, columns are effects

  1. The issued sheet94 causes × 12 effects on one A3 drawing
  2. Across a row, down a columnwhat one cause does; what closes one valve
  3. One row step by stepcause, delay, effects, first-out, reset

Step 1 · the issued sheet

What does the C&E drawing look like?

6 trip rows (red tags), 81 alarm rows from 48 alarm tags, 7 sequence rows. The top row of the effects gives the action: C close, OFF, MAN 0 %, TP/RS, ABORT.

Step 2 · interactive · the matrix

What does one cause do, and what closes one valve?

Click a row (cause) or a column head (effect).

Step 3 · interactive · row 002

How do you read row 002, FSL-105A?

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • Read across a row for everything one cause does; read down a column for every cause of one action.
  • All six trip rows give the same ten effects: both fuel SDVs close and the fuel loops go to MAN 0 %.
  • A missing X is a missing protection; an extra X is a spurious shutdown.
2

Part 2

Does the operator get a warning before the trip?

Part 2 · the plan

An alarm buys time to act

  1. Pre-alarms of the tripshow much time lies between the alarm and the trip
  2. The 81 alarm rowswhere in the unit the alarms sit

Step 1 · interactive · pre-alarm margin

How long does the operator have after the alarm?

time between alarm and trip$t = \dfrac{|x_{alarm} - x_{trip}|}{\text{rate}} + t_{delay}$

Step 2 · interactive · alarm rows

Which instruments carry the 81 alarm limits?

Click a bar.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • Each trip has a pre-alarm on the safe side: FAL 51.3 before FSL 40 m³/h; TI-1007 H 393 °C and TIC-101 H 395 °C before TSHH 410 °C.
  • The faster the approach, the less time the alarm gives; a sudden loss of flow leaves seconds.
  • Alarm rows only alarm; most are suppressed with no feed.
3

Part 3

How does the heater restart, and is the sheet right?

Part 3 · the plan

A latched trip and a checked sheet

  1. The restart sequencereset, purge, light-off and oil: the purple rows
  2. Checks against the simulator36 checks, each computed from the model

Step 1 · interactive · permissives

Which permissive is holding the restart?

Tick the conditions that hold

Step 2 · interactive · checks

How do we know the sheet matches the logic?

36 of 36 checks pass in the tab.

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • A trip latches: reset, a 120 s purge with five permissives, light-off on gas at 3–15 %, then oil once PDC-111 ≥ 150 kPa.
  • The sheet is checked against the model: settings, delays, alarm limits and every effect of a real trip.
  • Relief valves are mechanical, so they are not causes on this sheet.

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Read across a row for what a cause does, down a column for what causes an action.

2

Look for the first-out to find which cause tripped the heater.

3

Act on the pre-alarm: it is the time the trip leaves you.

4

Never bypass a permissive to restart faster; clear the cause, reset, purge.
